newsitem.title: UK: IPE April Brent crude ends Monday slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: IPE April Brent crude ends Monday slightly firmer.

text.p: April Brent crude on the IPE futures ended the day in positive territory after recovering over 15 cents in the last quarter hour of trade on the back of a NYMEX-led upward push, brokers said.

"Brent kept trying to recover (in late trade) but the NYMEX guys came and put a cap on it (WTI futures) every time it tried to push upwards. Then they made a break for the upside and we (IPE Brent) followed," one U.K. based broker said.
"It (the late upward move) was as much based on fear as anything else - fear of seeing the same as we saw on Friday when markets lost a lot of ground," another broker commented.
April Brent closed on Monday up seven cents at $18.92 a barrel. Next support was seen around $18.68 followed by $18.50 a barrel. April WTI ended down some four cents at $20.26 a barrel.

Some traders saw world markets fundamentally oversupplied with crude oil and, although technicals pointed to a recovery following last weeks sell-off, fundamentals could push prices in the opposite direction.
"There's just too much crude around and (refining) margins are awful. Why should prices go up?" one trader of North Sea crudes said.
Futures brokers pointed to a cold spell hitting the New York area which might give some support to levels.
"It's started to snow over there (New York) so maybe this will help keep prices up, but there was a strong drive for much of today to push it (April WTI) below $20 (a barrel)," one said.
The contract hit an intraday low of $19.96 on Monday.

Brent April and May contracts saw average volume trade but further forward levels dropped sharply in thin action. June lost some 12 cents to close at $18.52 and July ended down 15 cents at $18.43 a barrel.
March IPE gas oil closed earlier down some $2.25 a tonne at $160.25 and, based on the Brent IPE close, brokers expected the contract to open up $1-$1.50 a tonne on Tuesday.
